title: Best 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (2026): 5 Verified Picks
h1: The Best 50-Pint Dehumidifiers with a Built-In Pump
dek: Full-size capacity, no bucket to haul: these 50-pint pump models push water up to a sink or out a window so the basement stays dry while you get on with your life.
description: The best 50 pint dehumidifier with pump picks from Frigidaire, hOmeLabs, GoveeLife, Hisense and Waykar, plus how to spot pump model numbers and set one up.
intro: A **50 pint dehumidifier with pump** is the workhorse most damp basements actually need. Fifty pints a day under the current DOE test is the largest portable size sold, and the built-in condensate pump means you never carry a sloshing bucket up the stairs again. The pump pushes water through a thin hose up to a laundry sink, a window or a drain line overhead, so the unit can run all summer without a single trip downstairs.

The trouble is that almost every brand sells its 50-pint model in two versions — one with a pump and one without — and the model numbers differ by a single letter. Below are the pump-equipped 50-pint units we can verify on Amazon, how to tell the pump versions apart at a glance, and the setup details that decide whether a pump unit runs for years or trips its error light in week two.
topPicksLead: For most basements without a floor drain, the **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1** is the best 50-pint dehumidifier with a pump: full DOE 2019 capacity, a set-a-number humidistat, and the flexibility to drain by pump, gravity hose or bucket.

blocks.text: That middle number is why a pump is worth the premium. A gravity hose only works if the drain sits below the unit’s outlet; a pump can push water up to a utility sink, across a joist to a drain stack, or out a basement window.

sections.heading: How we pick 50-pint dehumidifiers with pumps

blocks.text: We don’t run a test lab. We compare models on the data that’s consistent across brands: pint ratings under the 2019 DOE procedure, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals for drainage options and humidistat range, and CPSC recall records. Then we read owner reviews for patterns — pumps that fail early, sensors that throw error codes, hoses that pop off.

For this guide, every pick had to be a genuine 50-pint-class unit with a built-in pump and a verified Amazon listing. We weighted dependable drainage highest, then honest capacity ratings, efficiency and remote monitoring. Models with recall histories or capacity claims we couldn’t reconcile were left out.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 50-pint dehumidifier with a pump

items.label: A DOE 2019 rating
items.text: Check that “50 pints” is the DOE figure. Listings that headline 70, 137 or 150 pints are quoting older or saturated-air tests; the ENERGY STAR database shows the comparable number.

items.label: Rated pump lift
items.text: Measure from the floor to your sink rim or window sill and add a foot for the hose loop. Most built-in pumps handle about 15 feet, which covers nearly any basement.

items.label: Three ways to drain
items.text: The best units let you choose pump, gravity hose or bucket, so a pump failure doesn’t take the whole machine out of service.

items.label: Auto-restart
items.text: A pump unit usually runs unattended. Auto-restart brings it back at the same settings after a power blip.

items.label: Alerts or an app
items.text: If the pump stalls, a smart model can tell you before the basement climbs back above 60%. Otherwise, pair it with a [Wi-Fi hygrometer](/best/best-hygrometer/).

items.label: ENERGY STAR
items.text: A 50-pint unit draws roughly 500 watts while running. Over a season, an efficient model saves real money.

blocks.text: Midea Cube 50 vs. Midea's pump model

The Midea Cube 50 we feature in our [best 50-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/) guide is the standard version: it drains into a big base reservoir or a gravity hose. Midea's 50-pint pump model is a separate, conventional upright unit rather than a Cube; if you need lift, make sure “pump” appears in the listing title before you check out.

Honeywell and GE both have current 50-pint pump models on Amazon — the TPFIT50PWK and GE’s 50-pint with pump, both picks above. Whirlpool and Pelonis have sold 50-pint pump models too, and GE’s older APYR50LC still turns up on clearance; we couldn’t verify current Amazon listings for those, so they aren’t cards here — but the same buying rules apply.

sections.heading: How to set up a dehumidifier pump so it keeps working

items: **Run it on the bucket first.** Give the unit a day to confirm the compressor and humidistat work before you add the pump hose.
**Route the hose without kinks.** Use the supplied pump line, keep bends gentle, and secure the end in the sink or drain so it can’t whip out.
**Stay within the rated lift.** Measure the vertical rise, not the hose length. Long horizontal runs are fine; extra height is what strains the pump.
**Switch the pump on in the menu.** Many models default to bucket mode until you press the pump button.
**Clean the pump reservoir monthly in season.** Basement air carries dust and biofilm; a quick rinse prevents most pump error codes.
**Check the outlet in winter.** A hose that exits outdoors can freeze; route it to an indoor drain when temperatures drop.

blocks.title: If the pump light comes on
blocks.text: Unplug, empty the bucket, and check the hose for kinks or a clog at the outlet. If the error returns, our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide walks through the next steps — including when to fall back to the gravity hose.

sections.heading: Is a 50-pint pump unit the right size?

blocks.text: Fifty pints suits a basement over about 1,500 square feet, any space with seepage or sweating walls, or a smaller area next to a laundry room or shower. For a single damp room it’s overkill; a 35-pint unit cycles less. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the full chart, and if one 50-pint unit can’t keep up, consider a [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) rather than a second portable.

If your basement has no drain below the unit, a 50-pint dehumidifier with a pump is the most practical upgrade you can make. The **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1** is the safest all-round choice, the **hOmeLabs** pump-and-Wi-Fi model is the budget route, the **GoveeLife** is the pick if you want your phone to tell you when something goes wrong, the **GE 50-Pint with Pump** comes with its hose and a stated 15-foot lift, and the **Honeywell TPFIT50PWK** suits a basement laundry area. Whatever you choose, read the model number carefully — one letter decides whether you get the pump — and set the humidistat to about 45–50% using our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/).

faqs.q: What is the best 50 pint dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: For most basements, the Frigidaire FFAP5033W1. It’s rated at 50 pints a day under the current DOE test and lets you drain by pump, gravity hose or bucket. The hOmeLabs 50-pint with pump and Wi-Fi is the budget alternative.

faqs.q: Does the Midea Cube 50 pint dehumidifier have a pump?
faqs.a: The Cube 50 drains into its base reservoir or a gravity hose. Midea’s 50-pint pump model is a separate, conventional upright unit rather than a Cube, and its listing title says “with pump.” Check the exact listing before ordering.

faqs.q: Is the hOmeLabs 50 pint dehumidifier with pump any good?
faqs.a: Yes, for the money. Amazon lists it at 50 pints a day with a built-in pump, Wi-Fi app control and a coverage claim of up to 7,500 square feet, and it has a large base of owner reviews. Treat the listing’s 120-pint figure as a saturated-air number and compare it with rivals on the 50.

faqs.q: Does the Frigidaire 50 pint dehumidifier with built-in pump have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Frigidaire combines a pump and Wi-Fi in its Gallery model, the FGAC5044W1. The FFAP5033W1 we recommend is the straightforward pump model; pair it with a Wi-Fi hygrometer if you want phone alerts.

faqs.q: Is the GE 50-pint dehumidifier with built-in pump still sold?
faqs.a: Yes. GE’s current 50-pint with pump is on Amazon with a 16-foot hose and a rated 15-foot vertical lift, and it’s one of our picks above. The older APYR50LC is discontinued and mostly turns up on clearance.

faqs.q: How high can a 50-pint dehumidifier pump water?
faqs.a: Most residential built-in pumps are rated for roughly 15–16 feet of vertical lift, which reaches a sink, window or overhead drain in nearly any basement. Check the manual for your model’s exact figure.
